## Overview

LRP308 is a **one-knob companion** to [LRP198](../lrp-rli-mech-198/): the same rows,
outcome, own-baseline term, adjustment set, subject random intercept and priors,
differing in exactly one thing. Where LRP198 adjusts for measured ability with
`blocks` (WPPSI-III Block Design) alone, this fit uses the two-subtest composite
`objass_c` — Block Design plus Object Assembly.

The ability-adjusted panel LRP196–201 is the project's evidence that the letter-sound
association is not merely measured ability, and its obvious rebuttal is that it adjusts
for a single noisy subtest. Over the 54 analysed children the two subtests correlate at
0.664, so Block Design alone is roughly a 0.66-reliable measure of what they share while
their sum is roughly 0.80-reliable. This fit re-reads the same comparison at the higher
reliability, so the rebuttal has a fitted answer.

Role in the panel: **an oral-language negative control**.

A better-measured proxy is still a proxy. Both subtests are perceptual-organisation
tasks, so what they share is a **narrow visuospatial factor** — the domain of relative
strength in the Down syndrome profile — and not the latent general ability `GA` of the
project's causal diagram, which stays unmeasured and structurally unblockable. Adjusting
for the composite does not move the mechanism slope any closer to a causal quantity: it
remains an **adjusted association**.

## How to read it

Compare with **LRP198**, not with the unadjusted LRP98. A slope that holds up here
having held up there is adjusted for the shared visuospatial variance about as well as
this battery permits. A slope that shrinks here but not there was carrying
subtest-specific noise. A screening regression over the fitted rows put the difference at
well under a tenth of a standard error, so **agreement is the expected result** — the
purpose is to close a line of criticism, not to report a new effect.

## Model

$$
\eta = \alpha + \alpha_{\text{phase}} + \beta_G G
  + \beta_{\text{mech}}\, z(\operatorname{logit}_* L_{\text{post}})
  + \gamma_{\text{own}}\operatorname{logit}_*(E_{\text{pre}})
  + \gamma_A z(A) + \gamma_{\text{objass}} z(\text{objass\_c})
  + \sum_c \gamma_c z(c) + u_{\text{child}}.
$$

The only difference from LRP198 is that $\gamma_{\text{blocks}} z(\text{blocks})$ is
replaced by $\gamma_{\text{objass}} z(\text{objass\_c})$. The composite is the raw sum of
the two subtests, derived by
`statistical_models.preprocessing.derive_nonverbal_ability_composite`; the subtests have
near-equal spread in this cohort, so the sum agrees with the average of their
standardised scores to a correlation of 0.99984, and it is standardised here in any case.
